name: Hot Glass Alley
unique: A working glass studio in NoDa where you pick a color, sit at the bench and blow your own bowl or ornament with an instructor guiding your hands the whole way.
buzz: The instructors keep it safe and funny, and you leave with something heavy and real. Book two weeks out for weekends.

name: Penland School of Craft
unique: A craft school on a mountain that has taught glass, clay, metal and textiles since 1929, with intensive workshops and housing on campus in the woods.
buzz: People describe it as summer camp for adults with serious skills; classes fill months out. The glass studio is the hardest to get into.

name: Jackson County Green Energy Park
customer: Beginners, families with teens, curious people
unique: A glassblowing studio heated by methane captured from a closed landfill, where you make a paperweight or ornament in a workshop that is half craft class and half waste to energy tour.
buzz: The story is as good as the glass and the instructors explain the methane system while you work. Prices are low for a hot shop class.

name: Starworks
unique: A former hosiery mill turned glass studio and ceramics center in a small town, with classes, artist residencies and a cafe that locals treat as the town square.
buzz: The scale is surprising for a town of 800 and the classes are small; book ahead for glassblowing weekends.

name: Corning Museum of Glass
unique: The largest glass museum in the world, with a hot shop where you can make your own blown ornament or flameworked bead after walking through three thousand years of glass.
buzz: The make your own sessions sell out and are worth booking first; the museum alone is a half day. Kids can do it too.

name: Pittsburgh Glass Center
unique: A public access glass studio in a converted warehouse with classes in blowing, flameworking and casting, plus free gallery shows by resident artists.
buzz: The teaching is patient and the facility is serious; weekend intro classes are the gateway.

name: Brooklyn Glass
unique: A glassblowing studio in Gowanus where beginners make drinking glasses and vases in a two hour session, then pick them up after annealing.
buzz: The instructors are working artists and the classes are small; it is a popular date night, so book early.

name: Seattle Glassblowing Studio
unique: A hot shop near the waterfront where you can blow a float or a tumbler in a class, or watch a demo and buy work from local artists.
buzz: The make your own class is the draw and the staff are good with nervous beginners; pieces ship if you are traveling.

name: Arrowmont School of Arts and Crafts
unique: A craft school on a hill above Gatlinburg with workshops in wood, clay, fiber, metal and glass, and a gallery that is free to visit.
buzz: The setting is quiet even when the town below is packed and the instructors are nationally known; housing and meals are on campus.

name: Haystack Mountain School of Crafts
unique: A modernist campus on a granite ledge over the Atlantic, where intensive craft workshops run for decades and the architecture is as memorable as the classes.
buzz: People call it a pilgrimage; the location is remote and the schedule is intense. Scholarships exist and are worth asking about.

name: Peters Valley School of Craft
unique: A craft school in a former village inside the Delaware Water Gap, with blacksmithing, pottery, fiber and glass workshops and cabins along a creek.
buzz: The setting is beautiful and the classes are small; it is a quiet alternative to a big city workshop.

name: Touchstone Center for Crafts
unique: A craft campus in the Laurel Highlands with blacksmithing, glass, ceramics and wood workshops, plus lodging in cabins on the grounds.
buzz: The classes are affordable and the setting is woodsy; it is close to Ohiopyle and Fallingwater for a combined trip.

name: Snow Farm
unique: A craft school in the Berkshire foothills with glassblowing, blacksmithing, pottery and fiber workshops, plus affordable lodging and meals.
buzz: People come back yearly; the glass program is strong and the vibe is unpretentious.

name: The Crucible
unique: An industrial arts school where you can take a one day class in blacksmithing, welding, glass casting, neon or fire performance, with a faculty of working artists.
buzz: The classes are physical and well taught and the fire arts are the draw; wear cotton and closed shoes.

name: Artisan's Asylum
unique: A 100,000 square foot maker space with classes in welding, woodworking, robotics, glass and textiles, plus open studio time if you join.
buzz: The range of skills under one roof is the point and the instructors are practical; intro classes are cheap.

name: Baltimore Knife and Sword
unique: A working forge that makes swords and knives for film and museums, with day classes where you hammer out your own blade from a billet of steel.
buzz: You leave with a knife you made and a new respect for smiths; the instructors are patient with total beginners. Book well ahead.

name: Dragon's Breath Forge
unique: A forge in the Connecticut woods where you make a knife or a small blade in a day, with coal forges, anvils and instructors who teach the hammer rhythm first.
buzz: The day is physical and satisfying and the shop smells like coal and hot steel; classes fill months ahead.

name: The Steel Yard
unique: An industrial arts center on a former steel site with blacksmithing, welding, ceramics and jewelry classes, plus public art projects made by members.
buzz: The teaching is good and the space is honest; intro welding fills fast.

name: Charleston Cooks
unique: A hands on cooking school where you make shrimp and grits, she crab soup and benne wafers, then eat what you cooked with wine.
buzz: The classes are relaxed and the recipes are actually repeatable at home; book the lowcountry classics session.

name: Callie's Hot Little Biscuit
unique: A biscuit shop that grew out of a mail order business and now teaches biscuit making, with a counter of ham biscuits and pimento cheese worth the line.
buzz: The buttermilk biscuits are the benchmark and the classes are short and hands on; go early before the case empties.

name: Institute of Culinary Education
unique: A professional culinary school that opens its kitchens to the public for single classes in knife skills, pasta, pastry and bread, taught by chefs who work in restaurants.
buzz: The facilities are professional and the classes are efficient; you leave with technique, not just a recipe.

name: The Chopping Block
unique: A cooking school and shop where you make a full menu in a small group, from knife skills to braising, then sit down and eat it with the class.
buzz: The teaching is practical and the groups are friendly; date night classes book out.

name: Cook Street School of Culinary Arts
unique: A professional culinary school with a public recreation program, where you cook a three course menu in a real kitchen and drink wine while you do it.
buzz: The classes are hands on and the instructors are working chefs; the pasta and knife skills sessions are the favorites.

name: The Gourmandise School
unique: A baking and cooking school near the beach with classes in sourdough, croissants, pasta and seasonal cooking, taught in a bright open kitchen.
buzz: The pastry classes are the strongest and the small groups mean real attention; book the bread series if you want a skill.

name: Viking Cooking School
unique: A cooking school attached to a kitchen showroom where classes range from Delta tamales to steakhouse basics, with stations for each pair of cooks.
buzz: The equipment is excellent and the classes are relaxed; a good date night in a state people underestimate.

name: Murray's Cheese
unique: A Greenwich Village cheese shop with a classroom downstairs where you taste through six cheeses and learn why the same milk makes wildly different wheels.
buzz: The instructors are opinionated in the best way and the tasting is generous; the cheese 101 class sells out.

name: Museum of Neon Art
unique: A museum of neon signs and kinetic art that also teaches one day neon bending classes, where you shape glass tubing over a flame and leave with a glowing piece.
buzz: The class is the reason to go and the museum is a bonus; bending neon is harder and more fun than it looks.

name: Aftelier Perfumes
unique: A perfumer's studio where you smell raw materials and blend your own fragrance in a small workshop, then take home a bottle of something nobody else owns.
buzz: It is intimate and intensely sensory and the instructor explains the chemistry without jargon; a genuinely unusual gift.

name: Prey Taxidermy
unique: A working taxidermy studio that teaches small classes in mouse and bird taxidermy, with a focus on craft and natural history rather than shock.
buzz: People arrive squeamish and leave proud; the instruction is respectful and the results are surprisingly beautiful.

name: Fleishers Craft Butchery
unique: A whole animal butcher shop that teaches breaking down a chicken, a lamb or a pig, with classes that send you home with the cuts you made.
buzz: The instructors are skilled and the ethics of the shop are part of the lesson; the chicken class is the beginner friendly one.

name: Brooklyn Brainery
unique: A tiny classroom that runs cheap one off classes on everything from pickling to lock picking to the history of the subway, taught by anyone with something to teach.
buzz: The range is the appeal and the prices are low; classes are small and sell out fast.

name: Soaring NV Glider Rides
unique: A sailplane ride over the Carson Valley where the engine is a tow plane and the silence after release is the whole point, with the Sierra as the backdrop.
buzz: Pilots explain the thermals and let you take the stick; it is smoother and quieter than a small plane. Book the longer ride.

name: Point of the Mountain Paragliding
unique: A ridge south of Salt Lake where the wind is so reliable that tandem flights launch all day and you can start a licensing course on the same hill.
buzz: The view of the valley and the lake is enormous and the landing is gentler than people expect; morning air is smoothest.

name: Sky Combat Ace
unique: You fly the plane in a mock dogfight over the desert, with an instructor handling takeoff and landing while you pull Gs and chase another aircraft.
buzz: It is as close to fighter pilot as a civilian can get and the instructors keep it safe; the video package is worth it.

name: Drive a Tank
unique: An armoured vehicle park where you can drive a real tank, crush a car and fire a machine gun, run by people who take safety and fun equally seriously.
buzz: It is expensive and completely unforgettable; the car crush package is the one people book. Reservations required.
